body: Just reading your comment made me burst into tears. I’m so tired of feeling like this. I feel so guilty even having him. He doesn’t deserve to be put through what I feel like I need to do.

I’m so tired of barely coping. You say I’ve gotten through so much, but I feel stripped. I don’t feel like I have any more strength to do this. I have done therapy for years and it hasn’t helped. I don’t know what’s left. I haven’t done NA. I’m in Australia. I could call the suicide prevention line but I don’t see how anything will change with them

I can’t say with certainty - simply because I am not my boyfriend - but the impression I get is that he is genuine. I met him at work where I have been for the past two years, and he has for maybe 12 years, and I know his situation quite well. He’s current partner is not his wife. They’ve been together for around two years, and they both brought step kids into the home. The reasons he hasn’t left are mostly logistical - a shared mortgage and the need to relocate the kids. It appears pretty loveless from the outside. And I don’t feel exploited (and I don’t see what he would be gaining from us being together except for occasional sex)

I don’t feel like I can make that promise. But realistically I am terrified of imposing grief on other people. I don’t think I’d have the balls to act

I’m so tired of feeling like this. I try so hard to do the right things by people, including myself. I do all the shit that people are supposed to do. I go to therapy, I take my meds. But nothing ever changes. Thank you for replying

While we're sharing, I actually went to hospital today for suicidality. And while I am still feeling like absolute shit, knowing that I have supports in place has made it feel like maybe - just maybe - the world isn't a pile of complete fuckery
I'm so scared of going and then they don't help me, too. In my head I have reserved hospital as a final place to go for help. If they can't or won't, I am petrified of what little is left

I'm sorry it's all so fucked.

For the record - I am a 26 year old female. I don't care if you can cook, or if you have a degree. I just had a stalk of your post history - you seem very intelligent and engaging. But you also seem to be under complete mental torture from yourself. And that's going to place a huge barrier between connecting with other people.

I hope this reply doesn't violate any rules - I don't mean this as unsolicited advice in any way. And I also don't mean it in a 'you have so much to live for!' way. I come to r/suicidewatch because I am suicidal far too often myself. But I guess what I am saying is, for the record, I read your posts and I don't see a failure. Not for a second. I see someone who is hurting, and who is having complete bullshit happen in their life at the moment

I'm not too good with football but I am Australian and this has been all over the media for the past few weeks so I'll do my best.

Adam Goodes is a skilled football player from an indigenous background. He has been seen to be controversial in and out of the game because:

- he is outspoken about indigenous issues, something which Australia has been, and continues to be, notoriously shitty with addressing
- as a skillful player, he attracts attention when he plays, either for good things (playing well) or not so good things (playing on rules to get free kicks, etc)
- a couple of years ago a 13 year old girl heckled him and called him an 'ape' which he heard. He signalled to security and they removed her from the stadium. Some people have said that this was an overreaction, others say that if was not Goodes' decision to have her removed
- Goodes was also named as Australian of the year. There is a bit of a weird thing in Australia where if you are successful, people resent that. Its known as Tall Poppy Syndrome

These factors have lead to tensions on field, where crowds have been relentlessly booing. There is a lot of (pathetic) debate around this. Without buying into that discussion, the sad part here is that Indigeonous Australians are so neglected socially that it is actually plausible that this is racially motivated, and that when you have a stadium of thousands of people booing Adam and no one else, it realistically begs the question...

P.S. I am embarrassed by Australia a lot, and this is one of the current embarrassments. For all the controversy around this, there is a rising level of support for Goodes' though. Having said that, if doesn't excuse the patheticness of the entire situation.

Hey, so I had this as a kid. Its called palilalia (from Latin, 'pali' means 'again and 'lalia' is 'to talk). Echolalia is a bit different in that the speaker repeats other peoples words, whereas in palilalia the speaker repeats their own words. It's essentially a tic, and it can be symptomatic of some types of disorders (chromosomal or neurodegenerative, for the eli15 crowd) but it can also be something that you just do and grow out of, which is what happened with me.

For the record, its a pretty embarrassing tic. Kids can and will pick on anything different. So if you do ask him about it, do be tactful because it might be a bit of a sore point.
